q.q: Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God?
q.f: Even King Darius hoped that Daniel's God would rescue him.

q.q: Who was the mother of the prophet Samuel?
q.f: Samuel's name was linked to Hannah asking the Lord for him.

q.q: Which nephew of Abram pitched his tent towards Sodom?
q.f: Lot's father Haran had died in Ur of the Chaldeans.

q.q: Which woman judged Israel while sitting under a palm tree named after her?
q.f: She sat between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim.

q.q: Who killed the army commander Sisera with a tent peg?
q.f: Deborah had told Barak that the honour would go to a woman.

q.q: Which son of Jacob was sold by his brothers to traders heading for Egypt?
q.f: He was sold for twenty shekels of silver.

q.q: Who led Israel after Moses died?
q.f: Joshua had been Moses' attendant since his youth.

q.q: Which prophet went up to heaven in a whirlwind?
q.f: A chariot of fire and horses of fire separated him from Elisha.

q.q: Who was the first king anointed over Israel?
q.f: Saul called his own tribe of Benjamin the smallest tribe of Israel.

q.q: Whose wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt?
q.f: Jesus later told His listeners, 'Remember Lot's wife!' (Luke 17:32).

q.q: Who was the father of John the Baptist?
q.f: He could not speak until baby John had been named.

q.q: Who was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as an apostle?
q.f: The other man put forward was Joseph called Barsabbas.

q.q: Who prayed 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' while being stoned?
q.f: The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.

q.q: Which tax collector climbed a tree to see Jesus?
q.f: He was short, so he ran ahead and climbed the tree.

q.q: Which Moabite woman refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi?
q.f: Ruth became the great-grandmother of King David.

q.q: Which queen said 'If I perish, I perish' before going to the king?
q.f: Her cousin Mordecai had raised her as his own daughter.

q.q: Who was Moses' brother, sent to speak for him?
q.f: God said Aaron could speak well and would be glad to see Moses.

q.q: Which prophetess, Aaron's sister, led the women with a tambourine?
q.f: This was after Israel crossed the Red Sea on dry ground.

q.q: Who did Moses marry in Midian?
q.f: She was a daughter of the priest of Midian.

q.q: Whose great strength was linked to hair that had never been cut?
q.f: He had been a Nazirite to God from birth.

q.q: Who found out the secret of Samson's strength for the Philistines?
q.f: Each Philistine lord promised her 1,100 shekels of silver.

q.q: Which prophet told King David 'You are that man!'?
q.f: Nathan first told David a story about a rich man who took a poor man's lamb.

q.q: Which son of King Saul was David's closest friend?
q.f: Their souls were 'knit together'.

q.q: Which son of David had his head caught in an oak tree?
q.f: His mule kept going and left him hanging in midair.

q.q: Which king asked God for an understanding heart to judge the people?
q.f: God was pleased that he had not asked for riches or long life.

q.q: Which queen threatened to kill Elijah after Mount Carmel?
q.f: Elijah ran for his life and sat down under a broom tree.

q.q: Which king of Judah was eight years old when he began to reign?
q.f: In his reign the Book of the Law was found in the temple.

q.q: Who spent three days and three nights inside a great fish?
q.f: He had been running from God's call to go to Nineveh.

q.q: Which patriarch had twelve sons?
q.f: God also gave Jacob the name Israel.

q.q: Who sold his birthright to his brother for some stew?
q.f: Because the stew was red, Esau was also called Edom.

q.q: Who was the mother of Isaac?
q.f: Sarah was ninety years old when the promise of a son was given.

q.q: Who became the wife of Isaac?
q.f: Abraham's servant found her at a well near the city of Nahor.

q.q: Which of Jacob's wives was the mother of Joseph?
q.f: Rachel later died giving birth to Benjamin.

q.q: Which priest did the boy Samuel serve under?
q.f: In those days the word of the Lord was rare.

q.q: Which prophet was a sheepherder from Tekoa?
q.f: He also tended sycamore-fig trees.

q.q: Which prophet married a woman named Gomer?
q.f: His marriage became a picture of God's faithful love for Israel.

q.q: Who led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls in fifty-two days?
q.f: He had been cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes.

q.q: Which Persian king allowed the Jewish exiles to go home and rebuild the temple?
q.f: Isaiah had mentioned Cyrus by name long before (Isaiah 45:1).

q.q: Which king threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into a furnace?
q.f: He ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.

q.q: Which king saw a hand writing on the palace wall during a feast?
q.f: He was killed that very night.

q.q: Which Roman governor handed Jesus over to be crucified?
q.f: He washed his hands in front of the crowd.

q.q: At which high priest's house was Jesus questioned after His arrest in Matthew?
q.f: The scribes and elders had gathered there.

q.q: Who was forced to carry the cross of Jesus?
q.f: Mark tells us he was the father of Alexander and Rufus.

q.q: Which rich disciple from Arimathea buried Jesus?
q.f: He laid Jesus in his own new tomb cut in the rock.

q.q: Which Pharisee came to Jesus at night?
q.f: Jesus told him that he must be born again.

q.q: Which apostle was sitting at a tax booth when Jesus called him?
q.f: He got up and followed Jesus straight away.

q.q: Who was Simon Peter's brother?
q.f: Both were fishermen on the Sea of Galilee.

q.q: Which disciple said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks?
q.f: Eight days later Jesus showed him His hands and side.

q.q: Which couple lied about the money from land they sold?
q.f: Peter said they had lied not to men but to God.

q.q: Which married couple, tentmakers like Paul, worked with him in Corinth?
q.f: They had left Rome when Claudius ordered all Jews to leave.

q.q: Whose mother was Eunice and grandmother was Lois?
q.f: Paul praised the sincere faith that lived first in them.

q.q: Which dealer in purple cloth from Thyatira listened to Paul in Philippi?
q.f: She and her household were baptised.

q.q: Which devout man in the temple took baby Jesus in his arms?
q.f: It had been revealed to him that he would see the Lord's Christ before he died.

q.q: Who lived 969 years, longer than anyone else in the Bible?
q.f: He was the grandfather of Noah.

q.q: Who walked with God and then 'was no more, because God had taken him away'?
q.f: Hebrews 11 says he was taken so that he did not see death.

q.q: Which boy heard God call his name in the night?
q.f: Eli told him to answer, 'Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening.'

q.q: Whose donkey spoke to him?
q.f: The donkey had seen the angel of the Lord standing in the road.

q.q: Which left-handed judge delivered Israel from King Eglon of Moab?
q.f: He was from the tribe of Benjamin.

q.q: Who was the father of King David?
q.f: Jesse lived in Bethlehem and had eight sons.

q.q: In which place did God plant a garden for the first man?
q.f: Genesis says the garden was 'in the east'.

q.q: Where did God confuse the language of the whole world?
q.f: The people had wanted to build a tower reaching to the heavens.

q.q: On which mountains did Noah's ark come to rest?
q.f: It came to rest on the seventeenth day of the seventh month.

q.q: On which mountain did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?
q.f: The Lord came down to the top of the mountain and called Moses up.

q.q: On which mountain did Elijah face the prophets of Baal?
q.f: There were 450 prophets of Baal against one prophet of the Lord.

q.q: In which town were Naomi and Ruth living when Ruth met Boaz?
q.f: They arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.

q.q: Which prophet named Bethlehem as the birthplace of a ruler over Israel?
q.f: Matthew quotes this verse when the wise men ask where Christ will be born.

q.q: In which town did Jesus grow up?
q.f: He was called a Nazarene because of it.

q.q: Where did Jesus turn water into wine at a wedding?
q.f: John calls this the first of Jesus' signs.

q.q: In which village did Lazarus, Mary and Martha live?
q.f: Bethany was less than two miles from Jerusalem.

q.q: In which garden did Jesus pray on the night He was arrested?
q.f: He asked Peter, James and John to keep watch with Him.

q.q: What does Luke call the place where Jesus was crucified?
q.f: Matthew, Mark and John give its Hebrew name, Golgotha.

q.q: Saul met the risen Jesus on the road to which city?
q.f: A light from heaven flashed around him.

q.q: Where were the disciples first called Christians?
q.f: Barnabas and Saul taught there for a full year.

q.q: In which city did Paul speak at the Areopagus about an altar 'to an unknown god'?
q.f: The altar inscription is mentioned in the next verse.

q.q: On which island was John when he received the visions of Revelation?
q.f: He was there because of the word of God and his testimony about Jesus.

q.q: Whose walls collapsed after Israel marched around the city?
q.f: The people shouted when the rams' horns sounded.

q.q: Which great city was Jonah sent to warn?
q.f: Jonah 3 says it took three days to go through it.

q.q: Where was Jonah's ship heading when he ran from God?
q.f: He boarded the ship at the port of Joppa.

q.q: From which city did Abram's family set out for Canaan?
q.f: They stopped and settled in Haran on the way.

q.q: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of a stairway to heaven?
q.f: Bethel means 'house of God'; the town had been called Luz.

q.q: Near which Samaritan town did Jesus meet a woman at Jacob's well?
q.f: Jacob had given the land nearby to his son Joseph.

q.q: What was the name of the pool with five colonnades where Jesus healed a man who had been ill for 38 years?
q.f: It was near the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem.

q.q: In which pool did Jesus tell a man born blind to wash?
q.f: John explains that Siloam means 'Sent'.

q.q: In Jesus' parable, the Good Samaritan helped a man on the road from Jerusalem to where?
q.f: Robbers had beaten the man and left him half dead.

q.q: In which river was Jesus baptised?
q.f: John baptised Him there.

q.q: In which Roman colony did Paul meet Lydia?
q.f: It was the leading city of that district of Macedonia.

q.q: After Athens, Paul went to which city and met Aquila and Priscilla?
q.f: Paul later wrote at least two letters to the church there.

q.q: On which island was Paul shipwrecked on his way to Rome?
q.f: A viper fastened on his hand there, but he was not harmed.

q.q: In which valley did Israel's army camp when David fought Goliath?
q.f: The Philistines were camped on the hill opposite.

q.q: To which Philistine city was Samson taken after his capture?
q.f: There he was made to grind grain in the prison.

q.q: Where did King Saul consult a medium?
q.f: Saul had earlier removed mediums from the land.

q.q: In which region of Egypt did Jacob's family settle?
q.f: There they became fruitful and grew greatly in number.

q.q: Which two store cities did the Israelite slaves build for Pharaoh?
q.f: The Egyptians put slave masters over them.

q.q: By which river was Ezekiel when the heavens opened and he saw visions of God?
q.f: He was among the exiles in Babylon.

q.q: In which citadel did King Xerxes reign in the book of Esther?
q.f: Nehemiah was also in the citadel of Susa when he heard about Jerusalem.

q.q: Which river did Israel cross on dry ground to enter the Promised Land?
q.f: The priests carrying the ark stood firm in the middle of the river.

q.q: Which lakeside town did Jesus make His home after leaving Nazareth?
q.f: It was in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.

q.q: What other name does John give for the Sea of Galilee?
q.f: The Old Testament calls it the Sea of Chinnereth.

q.q: To which village were two disciples walking when the risen Jesus joined them?
q.f: It was about seven miles from Jerusalem.

q.q: The queen of which land came to test Solomon with hard questions?
q.f: She came with camels carrying spices, gold and precious stones.

q.q: Melchizedek was king of which city?
q.f: He brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram.

q.q: In which river did Elisha tell Naaman to wash seven times?
q.f: Naaman first thought the rivers of Damascus were better.

q.q: On which road did Philip meet the Ethiopian official?
q.f: The official was reading from the prophet Isaiah in his chariot.

q.q: Where was John baptising when priests and Levites came to ask who he was?
q.f: This is a different Bethany from the village of Lazarus.

q.q: What did God create first, on the first day?
q.f: God called the light 'day' and the darkness 'night'.

q.q: What did God do on the seventh day of creation?
q.f: This later became the pattern for Israel's Sabbath.

q.q: Who ate the forbidden fruit first in the garden?
q.f: She then gave some to her husband, who was with her.

q.q: Who killed his brother Abel?
q.f: Abel was a keeper of sheep and Cain worked the soil.

q.q: For how long did rain fall during Noah's flood?
q.f: The waters went on covering the earth for 150 days.

q.q: What sign did God give Noah as a promise never to flood the whole earth again?
q.f: God called it the sign of His covenant with the earth.

q.q: What did Abraham offer on Mount Moriah instead of Isaac?
q.f: The ram was caught by its horns in a thicket.

q.q: What did Jacob see in his dream at Bethel?
a: Angels going up and down to heaven
q.f: God promised to give the land to him and his descendants.

q.q: Who did Jacob wrestle with until daybreak?
q.f: Afterwards Jacob said he had seen God face to face.

q.q: What special gift did Jacob make for Joseph?
q.f: Joseph was the son of Jacob's old age.

q.q: What did Pharaoh's dreams of seven fat and seven thin cows mean?
a: Seven years of plenty, then seven of famine
q.f: Joseph said God was showing Pharaoh what He was about to do.

q.q: How did God first speak to Moses at Mount Horeb?
a: Through an angel at a well
q.f: The bush was on fire but was not burnt up.

q.q: What did the Israelites put on their doorframes on the night of the first Passover?
q.f: God said He would pass over every house marked with the blood.

q.q: What did God use to drive back the Red Sea all night?
q.f: The waters were divided and Israel crossed on dry ground.

q.q: What did the Israelites call the bread from heaven in the wilderness?
q.f: When they first saw it, they asked one another, 'What is it?'

q.q: What did Moses strike at Horeb to give the people water?
q.f: He struck it in the sight of the elders of Israel.

q.q: What idol did Aaron make while Moses was on the mountain?
q.f: Moses was so angry he broke the tablets of the covenant.

q.q: How did the twelve spies describe the land of Canaan?
q.f: They brought back a cluster of grapes so big two men carried it on a pole.

q.q: What did Moses put on a pole so that bitten people could look at it and live?
q.f: Jesus compared this to Himself being lifted up (John 3:14).

q.q: How did Rahab help the two spies escape from Jericho?
a: She let them down by a rope through her window
She hid them in a well
She sent them out by boat
q.f: Her house was built into the city wall.

q.q: What stood still while Joshua's army defeated its enemies?
q.f: The sun stopped in the middle of the sky for about a full day.

q.q: What did Gideon put on the threshing floor to ask God for a sign?
q.f: The next night he asked God to do the opposite, and God did.

q.q: What did Gideon's 300 men carry into battle?
q.f: They shouted, 'A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!'

q.q: Where did David's stone hit Goliath?
q.f: David took five smooth stones from the stream.

q.q: What did David secretly cut from Saul's robe in a cave?
q.f: David refused to harm the Lord's anointed king.

q.q: What did David do when the ark was brought to Jerusalem?
a: He danced with all his might
q.f: He was wearing a linen ephod.

q.q: In which year of his reign did Solomon begin to build the temple?
q.f: It was 480 years after Israel came out of Egypt.

q.q: Which birds brought Elijah bread and meat by the brook?
q.f: They brought food every morning and evening.

q.q: What did the fire from God burn up on Mount Carmel?
a: The sacrifice, wood, stones and water
q.f: Elijah had water poured over the offering three times first.

q.q: What did Elisha make float after it fell into the Jordan?
q.f: The man had borrowed the axe, which is why he was so upset.

q.q: What sign did God give King Hezekiah that he would be healed?
a: A shadow went back ten steps
Rain fell on a dry fleece
q.f: God added fifteen years to Hezekiah's life.

q.q: What happened to Solomon's temple when Babylon captured Jerusalem?
a: It was turned into a palace
It was carried to Babylon stone by stone
q.f: The Babylonian commander also burnt the royal palace and the houses of Jerusalem.

q.q: How many men did Nebuchadnezzar see walking in the fiery furnace?
q.f: Only three men had been thrown in.

q.q: In whose reign was the second temple completed?
q.f: It was finished on the third day of the month of Adar.

q.q: How long did Ezra read the Book of the Law aloud to the people?
q.f: He read it in the square before the Water Gate.

q.q: What came to rest on each believer at Pentecost?
q.f: They began to speak in other languages.

q.q: About how many people were baptised after Peter's sermon at Pentecost?
q.f: They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to fellowship.

q.q: What fell from Saul's eyes when Ananias prayed for him?
q.f: Saul was then baptised.

q.q: How was Peter set free from Herod's prison?
a: An angel woke him and his chains fell off
q.f: At first Peter thought he was seeing a vision.

q.q: What happened while Paul and Silas sang hymns in the Philippian jail?
q.f: The jailer and his household believed and were baptised.

q.q: Which young man fell from a window while Paul preached late into the night?
q.f: Paul went down, embraced him and said he was alive.

q.q: What hid Jesus from the disciples' sight when He was taken up to heaven?
q.f: Two men in white said He would come back in the same way.

q.q: What happened to Haman in the end?
a: He was hanged on the gallows he built for Mordecai
He was thrown to the lions
He became the king's chief advisor
q.f: Esther then put Mordecai in charge of Haman's estate.

q.q: What did Job say after losing his children and possessions?
a: The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away
I will never trust God again
Take my life now, O LORD
q.f: Through all this Job did not sin or blame God.

q.q: In what form did the Spirit of God come down on Jesus at His baptism?
q.f: A voice from heaven said, 'This is My beloved Son.'

q.q: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before He was tempted?
q.f: He answered each temptation with words from Scripture.

q.q: Where did Mary lay baby Jesus after He was born?
q.f: There was no room for them in the inn.

q.q: Where did Mary and Joseph find the twelve-year-old Jesus after three days of searching?
q.f: He was listening to the teachers and asking them questions.

q.q: Which three gifts did the Magi bring to Jesus?
q.f: Matthew does not say how many Magi there were.

q.q: To which country did Joseph take Mary and Jesus to escape Herod?
q.f: An angel warned Joseph in a dream.

q.q: What did Jesus overturn in the temple courts?
q.f: He also overturned the seats of those selling doves.

q.q: What did Jesus do for His disciples at the Last Supper to show them how to serve?
q.f: Peter at first refused to let Jesus wash his feet.

q.q: How much were the chief priests willing to pay Judas?
q.f: Zechariah 11 also mentions thirty pieces of silver.

q.q: What did Jesus say would happen before the rooster crowed?
a: Peter would deny Him three times
q.f: Peter insisted he would never deny Him.

q.q: How did Judas show the crowd which man was Jesus?
a: He held a lamp to His face
q.f: He greeted Him with the words 'Greetings, Rabbi!'

q.q: What was the name of the high priest's servant whose ear Peter cut off?
q.f: Luke tells us Jesus touched the man's ear and healed him.

q.q: What was written on the charge above Jesus' head on the cross?
a: This is Jesus, the King of the Jews
This is the Son of God
q.f: John says the sign was written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek.

q.q: To whom did Jesus say, 'Today you will be with Me in Paradise'?
q.f: The man had asked Jesus to remember him in His kingdom.

q.q: What did Jesus say just before He gave up His spirit in John's Gospel?
q.f: He had just received the sour wine.

q.q: Who rolled the stone away from Jesus' tomb in Matthew?
q.f: The guards shook with fear and became like dead men.

q.q: What did Mary Magdalene call Jesus when she recognised Him at the tomb?
q.f: Rabboni means 'Teacher'.

q.q: How many times did the risen Jesus ask Peter, 'Do you love Me?'
q.f: Each time Jesus told him to feed or shepherd His lambs and sheep.

q.q: Which two Old Testament figures appeared with Jesus at the transfiguration?
q.f: His face shone like the sun.

q.q: What did Jesus say He would make Peter and Andrew?
q.f: They left their nets at once and followed Him.

q.q: How does the Lord's Prayer begin?
q.f: Jesus taught it in the Sermon on the Mount.

q.q: What did Jesus say when the disciples tried to keep children away from Him?
a: Let the little children come to Me
Send them home to their parents
q.f: He took the children in His arms and blessed them.

q.q: What did the crowd wave when Jesus rode into Jerusalem in John's Gospel?
q.f: They shouted 'Hosanna!'

q.q: What animal did Jesus ride into Jerusalem?
q.f: This fulfilled the words of the prophet Zechariah.

q.q: Why did the people of Nazareth try to throw Jesus off a cliff?
a: They were furious at His teaching in the synagogue
He healed on the Sabbath there
q.f: Jesus passed right through the crowd and went on His way.

q.q: Who said to Jesus, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God'?
q.f: Jesus said this had been revealed to him by the Father.

q.q: What did John the Baptist call Jesus?
q.f: He said Jesus takes away the sin of the world.

q.q: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus a person must be to see the kingdom of God?
q.f: Nicodemus asked how a grown man could be born again.

q.q: What did Jesus ask the Samaritan woman at the well for?
q.f: Jews did not usually associate with Samaritans.

q.q: Which sister sat at Jesus' feet listening while the other was busy serving?
q.f: Jesus said Mary had chosen the good portion.

q.q: In Luke 7, what did a sinful woman use to wipe Jesus' feet?
q.f: She also anointed His feet with perfume.

q.q: In whose name did Jesus tell His disciples to baptise?
a: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit
q.f: This command is often called the Great Commission.

q.q: Over how many days did the risen Jesus appear to His followers before ascending?
q.f: He spoke to them about the kingdom of God.

q.q: When did the Emmaus disciples recognise Jesus?
q.f: Their eyes were opened and He vanished from their sight.

q.q: Who asked Jesus, 'What is truth?'
q.f: He then told the crowd he found no basis for a charge against Jesus.

q.q: What did Jesus cry out at about the ninth hour on the cross?
a: My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?
Into Your hands I commit My spirit
Today you will be with Me
q.f: These words begin Psalm 22.

q.q: About how old was Jesus when He began His ministry?
q.f: People thought He was the son of Joseph.

q.q: What new name did Jesus give Simon when they first met?
q.f: Cephas is translated as Peter, which means 'rock'.

q.q: According to Jesus, what is the greatest commandment?
a: Love the Lord your God with all your heart
q.f: The second, He said, is to love your neighbour as yourself.

q.q: Finish Jesus' words: 'I am the way and the truth and ...'
q.f: He said this to Thomas, who asked how they could know the way.

q.q: Which 'I am' saying did Jesus speak about the world?
a: I am the light of the world
I am the bread of the world
I am the king of the world
I am the hope of the world
q.f: Whoever follows Him will never walk in darkness.

q.q: What does the good shepherd do for the sheep, according to Jesus?
a: Lays down His life for them
q.f: Jesus said He knows His sheep and they know Him.

q.q: To whom did Jesus say, 'I am the resurrection and the life'?
q.f: He said it before raising her brother Lazarus.

q.q: In which town's synagogue did Jesus read from the scroll of Isaiah in Luke 4?
q.f: It was His custom to go to the synagogue on the Sabbath.

q.q: What happened to Jesus' sweat as He prayed in anguish on the Mount of Olives?
a: It became like drops of blood
q.f: An angel from heaven came to strengthen Him.

q.q: What happened to Jesus' face at the transfiguration?
a: His face shone like the sun
His face was hidden by a veil
His face became like a lion's
His face was covered in dust
q.f: His clothes became as white as the light.

q.q: In the parable of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave to look for the lost one?
q.f: He calls his friends to rejoice when he finds it.

q.q: How many silver coins did the woman have before she lost one?
q.f: She lit a lamp and swept the house until she found it.

q.q: In the parable of the prodigal son, what animals did the younger son end up feeding?
q.f: He even longed to eat the pods the pigs were eating.

q.q: What did the father do when he saw his lost son coming home from far off?
a: Ran to him and embraced him
Sent a servant to meet him
q.f: He was filled with compassion.

q.q: Which gifts did the father give his returning son?
a: The best robe, a ring and sandals
A sword, a horse and a field
A crown, a cloak and a staff
q.f: He also ordered the fattened calf to be killed for a feast.

q.q: Where was the older brother when his younger brother came home?
q.f: He heard the music and dancing as he came near the house.

q.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who passed by first on the other side?
q.f: Next a Levite also passed by.

q.q: What did the Good Samaritan pour on the injured man's wounds?
q.f: He then took him to an inn on his own animal.

q.q: How many denarii did the Good Samaritan give the innkeeper?
q.f: He promised to repay any extra cost on his return.

q.q: What question led Jesus to tell the parable of the Good Samaritan?
q.f: An expert in the law asked it, wanting to justify himself.

q.q: In the parable of the sower, what ate the seed that fell on the path?
q.f: Jesus later explained that the seed on the path is someone who hears the message but does not understand it.

q.q: At most, how many times over did the seed on good soil multiply?
q.f: Other good soil produced sixty or thirty times as much.

q.q: Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is like which tiny seed that grows into a tree?
q.f: Birds come and nest in its branches.

q.q: In Jesus' parable, what did a woman mix into three measures of flour?
q.f: The leaven worked through all the dough.

q.q: What did the man do after finding treasure hidden in a field?
a: Sold all he had and bought the field
Told the owner of the field
q.f: He did it 'in his joy'.

q.q: What did the merchant sell everything to buy?
q.f: He had been searching for fine pearls.

q.q: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to a net that caught what?
q.f: The fishermen sorted the good fish from the bad.

q.q: Where did the wise man build his house?
q.f: He is the one who hears Jesus' words and acts on them.

q.q: Where did the foolish man build his house?
q.f: When the storm came, it fell, and great was its collapse.

q.q: In the parable of the ten virgins, how many were wise?
q.f: The wise ones took extra oil for their lamps.

q.q: What happened when the foolish virgins went to buy more oil?
a: The bridegroom came and the door was shut
They were given oil for free
q.f: Jesus ends with: 'Keep watch.'

q.q: What did the servant with one talent do with it?
a: Dug a hole and hid it
q.f: His master called him wicked and lazy.

q.q: What did the master say to the faithful servants in the parable of the talents?
a: Well done, good and faithful servant
q.f: He put them in charge of many things.

q.q: How much did each vineyard worker receive, even those hired at the eleventh hour?
q.f: The earliest workers grumbled that it was unfair.

q.q: How much did the unforgiving servant owe the king?
q.f: He would not forgive a fellow servant who owed him only a hundred denarii.

q.q: What did the rich fool plan to do with his large harvest?
a: Tear down his barns and build bigger ones
q.f: God told him that his life would be required of him that very night.

q.q: What was the name of the poor beggar at the rich man's gate?
q.f: He is a different Lazarus from the brother of Martha and Mary.

q.q: Where did the angels carry Lazarus the beggar when he died?
q.f: The rich man also died and was buried.

q.q: In Jesus' parable, which man prayed, 'God, have mercy on me, a sinner'?
q.f: Jesus said he went home justified.

q.q: In the parable of the persistent widow, what kind of judge did she keep pestering?
a: One who did not fear God or respect people
A judge who was her relative
q.f: Jesus told it to show that we should pray at all times and not lose heart.

q.q: What did the gardener ask for the fig tree that bore no fruit?
a: One more year to dig and fertilise it
To cut it down at once
To plant a new tree beside it
q.f: The owner had looked for fruit on it for three years.

q.q: In the parable of the two sons, which son actually went to work in the vineyard?
a: The one who first said no
q.f: He changed his mind and went.

q.q: At the king's wedding banquet, why was one guest thrown out?
a: He was not wearing wedding clothes
q.f: Jesus ends: 'Many are called, but few are chosen.'

q.q: Who did the master send for when the invited guests made excuses for not coming to his banquet?
a: The poor, crippled, blind and lame
q.f: One guest's excuse was that he had bought a field.

q.q: In the parable of the weeds, who sowed weeds among the wheat?
q.f: Jesus explained that the enemy is the devil.

q.q: What did the man in Jesus' parable ask his friend for at midnight?
q.f: The friend gave him what he needed because he kept asking.

q.q: In the parable of the tenants, what did the landowner build in his vineyard?
q.f: He also put a wall around it and dug a winepress.

q.q: According to Jesus' lesson from the fig tree, what do new leaves tell you?
q.f: He used it to teach about watching for the signs of His coming.

q.q: What does the shepherd separate in Jesus' picture of the final judgement?
q.f: The sheep had cared for 'the least of these'.

q.q: In Mark 4, what happens to the seed while the farmer sleeps?
q.f: The farmer does not know how it grows.

q.q: Why were the Pharisees grumbling just before Jesus told the parables of Luke 15?
a: He welcomed sinners and ate with them
q.f: His answer was the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son.

q.q: In Luke 15, what does the father say about his returning son?
a: He was dead and is alive again
He has earned his place again
He must work as a servant
He has paid for his mistakes
q.f: He says this to the older brother.

q.q: What was Jesus' first sign, at a wedding in Cana?
q.f: Through it His disciples believed in Him.

q.q: How many stone water jars did the servants fill at the wedding in Cana?
q.f: Each jar held twenty to thirty gallons.

q.q: What did a boy offer that Jesus used to feed five thousand men?
a: Seven loaves and a few fish
q.f: John notes that the loaves were made of barley.

q.q: How many baskets of leftovers were gathered after the feeding of the five thousand?
q.f: Women and children were fed as well as the five thousand men.

q.q: How many men were fed with seven loaves and a few small fish?
q.f: This was a separate meal from the feeding of the five thousand.

q.q: Which disciple walked on the water towards Jesus?
q.f: When he saw the wind he began to sink and cried, 'Lord, save me!'

q.q: What did Jesus say to calm the storm in Mark's Gospel?
q.f: The disciples asked, 'Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?'

q.q: How long had Lazarus been in the tomb when Jesus arrived?
q.f: Martha warned that by then there would be a smell.

q.q: Who was the blind beggar Jesus healed near Jericho?
q.f: He was the son of Timaeus.

q.q: Which synagogue leader asked Jesus to heal his dying daughter?
q.f: Jesus raised her, saying 'Talitha koum!'

q.q: What does 'Talitha koum' mean?
a: Little girl, I say to you, get up!
q.f: Jesus said it to Jairus' daughter.

q.q: What did Jesus say when He healed a deaf man in Mark 7?
q.f: He looked up to heaven and sighed deeply.

q.q: How long had the woman who touched Jesus' cloak been bleeding?
q.f: She had spent all her money on doctors.

q.q: How long had the man at the pool of Bethesda been an invalid?
q.f: Jesus told him, 'Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.'

q.q: How did four friends get a paralysed man to Jesus in a crowded house?
a: They lowered him through the roof
They carried him through a window
They asked the crowd to move
q.f: Jesus first told the man his sins were forgiven.

q.q: Of the ten lepers Jesus healed, how many came back to thank Him?
q.f: The one who returned was a Samaritan.

q.q: In which town did Jesus raise a widow's only son during his funeral?
q.f: A large crowd was with the grieving mother.

q.q: Whose servant did Jesus heal from a distance, praising his great faith?
q.f: Jesus said He had not found such faith even in Israel.

q.q: What name did the demons in the man from the Gerasenes give?
q.f: They said, 'for we are many'.

q.q: Into what animals did Jesus allow the demons called Legion to go?
q.f: About two thousand pigs rushed into the sea.

q.q: What did Jesus use to heal the man born blind in John 9?
q.f: He then sent him to wash in the Pool of Siloam.

q.q: How many fish were in the net when the disciples followed the risen Jesus' instructions?
q.f: Even with so many fish, the net was not torn.

q.q: Where did Jesus tell Peter he would find a coin to pay the temple tax?
q.f: The coin was enough for Jesus and Peter.

q.q: What happened to the fig tree Jesus cursed?
a: It was uprooted by the wind
q.f: Peter noticed it the next morning.

q.q: Whose mother-in-law did Jesus heal of a fever?
q.f: She got up at once and began to serve Him.

q.q: How long had the woman in the synagogue been bent over before Jesus healed her?
q.f: She immediately stood up straight and praised God.

q.q: What did Peter say to the lame man at the temple gate called Beautiful?
a: Silver or gold I do not have
Your faith has made you well
Take up your bed and go home
q.f: The man had been lame from birth.

q.q: Who did Peter raise to life in Joppa?
q.f: She was known for her kindness and charity, and was also called Dorcas.

q.q: What did people hope would fall on the sick as Peter passed by?
q.f: They laid the sick on cots and mats in the streets.

q.q: What happened when a viper bit Paul on Malta?
a: He shook it off and was not harmed
He became very ill for three days
He killed it with a stick
q.f: The islanders changed their minds and said he was a god.

q.q: In Lystra, what did the crowd call Paul and Barnabas after a lame man was healed?
q.f: Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes and stopped them offering sacrifices.

q.q: What did not run out for the widow of Zarephath while Elijah stayed with her?
q.f: It lasted just as the Lord had promised through Elijah.

q.q: Which prophet raised the son of the widow of Zarephath?
q.f: The Lord heard Elijah's prayer and the child lived.

q.q: What kept flowing for the prophet's widow until every jar was full?
q.f: Elisha told her to sell the oil and pay her debts.

q.q: How many times did the Shunammite woman's son sneeze when Elisha raised him?
q.f: Then the boy opened his eyes.

q.q: How many times did Naaman dip in the Jordan to be healed?
q.f: His skin became like that of a little child.

q.q: What happened when a dead man's body touched the bones of Elisha?
q.f: The man stood up on his feet.

q.q: What did Elisha's servant see when God opened his eyes at Dothan?
a: A great army of angels singing
q.f: They filled the hills all around Elisha.

q.q: What grew on Aaron's staff overnight?
q.f: It had sprouted, budded and blossomed too.

q.q: Into what did the water of the Nile turn in the first plague?
q.f: The fish in the river died.

q.q: How long did the plague of darkness cover Egypt?
q.f: Yet all the Israelites had light where they lived.

q.q: What did Elijah use to part the Jordan River?
q.f: Elisha later did the same with Elijah's cloak.

q.q: What did Moses throw into the bitter water at Marah to make it sweet?
q.f: The Lord showed him the piece of wood.

q.q: Who shut the lions' mouths so Daniel was not hurt?
q.f: Daniel was lifted out without a wound.

q.q: What could not be found on Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego after the furnace?
q.f: Not a hair on their heads was singed.

q.q: What did Paul's handkerchiefs and aprons do in Ephesus?
q.f: God was doing extraordinary miracles through Paul.

q.q: What does the name Immanuel mean?
q.f: Matthew links it to Isaiah's prophecy about a virgin bearing a son.

q.q: What does Golgotha mean?
q.f: It was the place where Jesus was crucified.

q.q: What did Samuel name the stone he set up, saying 'Thus far the LORD has helped us'?
q.f: He set it up after God gave Israel victory over the Philistines.

q.q: What new name did God give Jacob after he wrestled until daybreak?
q.f: It was given because he had struggled with God and with men and had prevailed.

q.q: Why did Pharaoh's daughter name the baby Moses?
a: She drew him out of the water
He was born by the river
He was a gift from God
q.f: She had found him in a basket among the reeds of the Nile.

q.q: Why did Adam name his wife Eve?
a: She would be the mother of all the living
She was made from his rib
She was the first to sin
q.f: Before this, Adam had called her 'woman'.

q.q: What did the name Ichabod announce?
a: The glory has departed from Israel
q.f: The ark of God had just been captured by the Philistines.

q.q: What name did Naomi ask to be called after returning from Moab?
q.f: She chose it because she felt the Almighty had dealt bitterly with her.

q.q: Why was Mary's son to be named Jesus, according to the angel?
a: He will save His people from their sins
He will be born in Bethlehem
He will be a great king
He will be called a Nazarene
q.f: The angel said this to Joseph in a dream.

q.q: Which Hebrew title is translated into Greek as 'Christ'?
q.f: Andrew told his brother Simon, 'We have found the Messiah.'

q.q: What does the name Barnabas mean?
q.f: He was a Levite from Cyprus whose real name was Joseph.

q.q: What nickname did Jesus give James and John?
q.f: In Aramaic the name is Boanerges.

q.q: In the writing on the wall, what did MENE mean?
a: God has numbered the days of your reign
You have been weighed and found wanting
q.f: Daniel explained all three words to King Belshazzar.

q.q: What did Abraham call the mountain where God provided a ram?
q.f: It is in the land of Moriah.

q.q: What does Akeldama mean?
q.f: The field was linked to the money Judas was paid.

q.q: In Revelation, Jesus calls Himself 'the Alpha and the Omega'. What does He say alongside it?
q.f: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet.

q.q: What does the name Abraham mean, according to Genesis 17?
q.f: Until then his name was Abram.

q.q: What did Rachel name her last son as she was dying, before Jacob renamed him Benjamin?
q.f: She died on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.

q.q: What does Corban mean in Mark 7?
q.f: Jesus used it to show how people avoided caring for their parents.

q.q: What does the word Rabbi mean?
q.f: Two of John the Baptist's disciples called Jesus by this title.

q.q: What is the Hebrew name of the Stone Pavement where Pilate sat in judgement?
q.f: It was there that Pilate said, 'Here is your King!'

q.q: Why was Hagar's son named Ishmael?
a: The LORD has heard your cry
The LORD has seen my affliction
q.f: The angel of the Lord met Hagar by a spring in the wilderness.

q.q: Why did Leah name her fourth son Judah?
a: This time I will praise the LORD
The LORD has seen my misery
God has given me a reward
Now my husband will love me
q.f: King David and Jesus both came from the tribe of Judah.

q.q: What did Lamech hope his son Noah would bring?
q.f: He hoped Noah would comfort them in the toil of working the cursed ground.

q.q: Why was the place called Gilgal, according to Joshua 5?
a: The LORD rolled away the reproach of Egypt
Twelve stones were set up there
q.f: Israel camped there after crossing the Jordan.

q.q: What does the name Nabal mean?
q.f: His wife Abigail said he lived up to his name.

q.q: What name did God send through Nathan for baby Solomon?
q.f: It was given because the Lord loved him.

q.q: Who did the Pharisees call 'the prince of demons'?
q.f: Jesus answered that a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand.

q.q: The Jewish feast of Purim gets its name from which word?
q.f: Haman had cast the pur, the lot, to choose a day to destroy the Jews.

q.q: What did Moses name the altar he built after the victory over the Amalekites?
q.f: Aaron and Hur had held up Moses' hands until sunset.

q.q: What did Gideon call the altar he built at Ophrah?
q.f: He built it after the angel of the Lord appeared to him.

q.q: What Babylonian name was Daniel given?
q.f: Belshazzar, with a similar name, was a later king.

q.q: Which apostle is described as 'Saul, who was also called Paul'?
q.f: From this point on Acts mostly calls him Paul.

q.q: What other name was Thomas known by?
q.f: Didymus means 'twin'.

q.q: What name was Gideon given after he tore down Baal's altar?
q.f: It means 'Let Baal contend with him'.

q.q: Which of these is listed as a fruit of the Spirit?
q.f: The list ends with gentleness and self-control.

q.q: In the armour of God, what is the sword of the Spirit?
q.f: Faith is the shield and salvation is the helmet.

q.q: Why did Esau say Jacob was 'rightly named'?
q.f: Jacob had taken both his birthright and his blessing.

q.q: What did Joseph name his firstborn son, saying God had made him forget his hardship?
q.f: His second son, Ephraim, was named because God made him fruitful.

q.q: What new name did God give to Sarai?
q.f: God promised that she would be the mother of nations.

q.q: In Revelation 16, why are the kings gathered at the place called Armageddon?
a: For battle on the great day of God
q.f: Armageddon is the place's name in Hebrew.

q.q: Why did Leah name her first son Reuben?
a: The LORD has seen my affliction
This time I will praise the LORD
q.f: He was the first of Jacob's twelve sons.

q.q: Which word did Adam use for Eve because she was taken out of man?
q.f: He called her 'bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh'.

q.q: How many commandments did God write on the two stone tablets?
q.f: They are listed in Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5.

q.q: How many apostles did Jesus choose?
q.f: Matthew lists them in pairs, beginning with Simon Peter and Andrew.

q.q: How many days and nights was Moses on the mountain with God?
q.f: He went up into the cloud on Mount Sinai.

q.q: For how many years did Israel eat manna in the wilderness?
q.f: It stopped when they reached the border of Canaan.

q.q: How many times did Israel march around Jericho on the seventh day?
q.f: On the other six days they marched around once a day.

q.q: How many people were saved in Noah's ark?
q.f: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives.

q.q: How old was Jesus when His parents found Him in the temple?
q.f: They had gone up to Jerusalem for the Passover feast.

q.q: How many times a day did Daniel pray towards Jerusalem?
q.f: He kept praying even after the king's decree was signed.

q.q: How old was Joseph when he was tending the flock and brought a bad report about his brothers?
q.f: He was the son of Jacob's old age.

q.q: How old was Joseph when he entered Pharaoh's service?
q.f: He then travelled throughout the land of Egypt.

q.q: How old was Joseph when he died?
q.f: His body was embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.

q.q: How old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
q.f: Sarah was ninety.

q.q: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
q.f: His nephew Lot went with him.

q.q: How old was Moses when he died?
q.f: His eyes were not weak and his strength was not gone.

q.q: How old was David when he became king?
q.f: He reigned for forty years.

q.q: How long did Jacob work for Laban to marry Rachel, in all?
q.f: The first seven years seemed like only a few days because of his love for her.

q.q: How many trained men did Abram take to rescue Lot?
q.f: They chased the enemy as far as Dan.

q.q: How many men did God choose to fight with Gideon?
q.f: They were the men who lapped the water.

q.q: How many stones did Joshua tell the twelve men to take from the Jordan?
q.f: They were a memorial for future generations.

q.q: How many smooth stones did David take from the brook to face Goliath?
q.f: He needed only one.

q.q: How long did it take Solomon to build the temple?
q.f: It was finished in the month of Bul.

q.q: How many proverbs did Solomon compose, according to 1 Kings?
q.f: His songs numbered a thousand and five.

q.q: How many years did God add to Hezekiah's life?
q.f: God also promised to defend Jerusalem from Assyria.

q.q: Over how many provinces did King Xerxes reign?
q.f: His empire stretched from India to Cush.

q.q: How many days did Jonah say were left before Nineveh would be overturned?
q.f: The people believed God and proclaimed a fast.

q.q: How many people were on board Paul's ship to Rome?
q.f: All of them reached land safely.

q.q: How many elders sit on thrones around God's throne in Revelation 4?
q.f: They wear white and have golden crowns.

q.q: To how many churches in Asia did John write in Revelation?
q.f: Ephesus is the first of them.

q.q: How many gates does the new Jerusalem have?
q.f: They bear the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.

q.q: According to the Jews, how many years had Herod's temple taken to build by Jesus' time?
q.f: Jesus was really speaking about the temple of His body.

q.q: How many times did Paul receive 'forty lashes minus one'?
q.f: He also says he was beaten with rods three times.

q.q: How old was Adam when he died?
q.f: Only Methuselah, Jared and Noah are recorded as living longer.

q.q: How many times did Elijah send his servant to look for rain clouds?
q.f: The seventh time a small cloud appeared.

q.q: How many springs did Israel find at Elim?
q.f: There were also seventy palm trees.

q.q: With what did Samson strike down a thousand men?
q.f: The jawbone was still fresh.

q.q: How many demons had gone out of Mary Magdalene?
q.f: She and other women supported Jesus' ministry.

q.q: How many generations does Matthew count from Abraham to David?
q.f: He counts fourteen more to the exile and fourteen to Christ.

q.q: How many believers were gathered when Peter spoke about replacing Judas?
q.f: They chose Matthias.

q.q: How long did Jesus stay where He was after hearing that Lazarus was sick?
q.f: By the time He arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days.

q.q: How many people in Israel had not bowed to Baal, God told Elijah?
q.f: Elijah had thought he was the only one left.

q.q: What is the number of the beast in Revelation 13?
q.f: John calls it a call for wisdom.

q.q: What is the first book of the Bible?
q.f: Genesis means 'beginning' or 'origin'.

q.q: What is the last book of the Bible?
q.f: It opens with 'The revelation of Jesus Christ'.

q.q: Which Gospel begins 'In the beginning was the Word'?
q.f: The opening words echo the first verse of Genesis.

q.q: Which book comes straight after the four Gospels?
q.f: Its writer calls Luke's Gospel 'my first book'.

q.q: To whom are both Luke's Gospel and Acts addressed?
q.f: Luke calls him 'most excellent Theophilus'.

q.q: Which book of the Bible has the most chapters?
q.f: It has 150 psalms; its last verse says 'Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!'

q.q: Which book tells how Israel left slavery in Egypt?
q.f: They left at the end of 430 years, to the very day.

q.q: Which book is the last in the Old Testament?
q.f: Malachi's name means 'my messenger'.

q.q: Which short letter asks a believer to welcome back a slave called Onesimus?
q.f: Paul wrote it while he was in chains.

q.q: Which book is introduced as 'Solomon's Song of Songs'?
q.f: It is a book of love poetry.

q.q: In which book do we read 'Love is patient, love is kind'?
q.f: Chapter 13 is often read at weddings.

q.q: Which book has a famous chapter about the heroes of faith, starting 'Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for'?
q.f: The chapter mentions Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Rahab and many more.

q.q: Which book says 'To everything there is a season'?
q.f: The passage goes on: 'a time to be born and a time to die'.

q.q: Which book is a set of poems mourning the fall of Jerusalem?
q.f: It begins: 'How lonely lies the city'.

q.q: Which book is about a blameless man from Uz who suffered greatly?
q.f: God speaks to Job out of a whirlwind near the end of the book.

q.q: Which book begins with God telling Moses to take a census of Israel?
q.f: The counting of the people gave the book its English name.

q.q: In which book does Moses die?
q.f: He died in the land of Moab after seeing the Promised Land from Mount Nebo.

q.q: Which book ends with 'everyone did what was right in his own eyes'?
q.f: It also says there was no king in Israel in those days.

q.q: Which book begins 'In the days when the judges ruled'?
q.f: It begins with a famine that drove a family from Bethlehem to Moab.

q.q: Which prophet saw a valley full of dry bones come to life?
q.f: God told him to prophesy to the bones.

q.q: In which letter did Paul write 'For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain'?
q.f: He wrote this letter while in chains.

q.q: In which letter do we read that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him?
q.f: Romans 8 ends by saying nothing can separate us from the love of God.

q.q: Which letter tells believers to put on the full armour of God?
q.f: The armour includes a belt of truth and a shield of faith.

q.q: Which letter says that faith without deeds is dead?
q.f: It uses Abraham and Rahab as examples of faith in action.

q.q: Which Old Testament book has only one chapter?
q.f: It is a vision about the nation of Edom.

q.q: Which of these New Testament letters has just one chapter?
q.f: Jude calls himself a brother of James.

q.q: Which is the shortest of the four Gospels?
q.f: It has sixteen chapters.

q.q: Which Gospel contains the Sermon on the Mount?
q.f: It runs from Matthew 5 to Matthew 7.

q.q: In which book is the prayer of Jabez found?
q.f: God granted his request.

q.q: Which book tells the story of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
q.f: They refused to worship the golden statue.

q.q: Which book contains the blessing 'The LORD bless you and keep you'?
q.f: God gave this blessing for Aaron and his sons to speak over Israel.

q.q: Which book contains the words 'Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One'?
q.f: Jesus quoted these words when asked about the greatest commandment (Mark 12:29).

q.q: Which book says 'Trust in the LORD with all your heart'?
q.f: It goes on: 'and lean not on your own understanding'.

q.q: In which Gospel does Jesus say 'I am the bread of life'?
q.f: John records seven 'I am' sayings with a picture, such as the vine and the gate.

q.q: Which letter says 'All Scripture is God-breathed'?
q.f: Paul wrote it to his young helper Timothy.

q.q: Which book ends with a vision of the new Jerusalem coming down out of heaven?
q.f: John saw the holy city prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.

q.q: Which book tells how Israel took possession of the Promised Land?
q.f: The land was divided among the tribes by lot.

q.q: According to Proverbs 1, the fear of the LORD is the beginning of what?
q.f: Proverbs 9:10 says it is also the beginning of wisdom.

q.q: What does Proverbs say a gentle answer does?
q.f: A harsh word, by contrast, stirs up anger.

q.q: According to Proverbs, what goes before destruction?
q.f: A haughty spirit goes before a fall.

q.q: Which creature does Proverbs tell the lazy person to watch and learn from?
q.f: The ant works without anyone commanding it.

q.q: Finish the proverb: 'As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens...'
q.f: Good friends help each other grow.

q.q: Proverbs 31 says a wife of noble character is worth far more than what?
q.f: The chapter goes on to describe her strength, work and kindness.

q.q: According to Proverbs 18, what is the name of the LORD like?
q.f: The righteous run to it and are safe.

q.q: What does Proverbs tell you to do if your enemy is hungry?
q.f: Paul quotes this in Romans 12.

q.q: What does Proverbs tell us to guard with all diligence, because life flows from it?
q.f: The heart in the Bible stands for our inner life and choices.

q.q: According to Proverbs 13, who becomes wise?
a: He who walks with the wise
q.f: The companion of fools, it says, will be destroyed.

q.q: What does Proverbs 3 say God will do if we acknowledge Him in all our ways?
q.f: It follows 'Trust in the LORD with all your heart'.

q.q: What does Proverbs 11 say happens to the person who refreshes others?
a: He will be repaid in gold
q.f: It also says a generous soul will prosper.

q.q: According to Ecclesiastes, what is the whole duty of man?
a: Fear God and keep His commandments
q.f: It is the writer's conclusion after all he has seen.

q.q: What does Ecclesiastes say is not quickly broken?
q.f: Two can stand together where one alone may be overpowered.

q.q: What does Ecclesiastes say there is nothing new under?
q.f: What has been will be again.

q.q: When does Ecclesiastes tell us to remember our Creator?
a: In the days of our youth
q.f: Before the days of trouble come.

q.q: In Psalm 119, God's word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my what?
q.f: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible.

q.q: What does Psalm 46 tell us to do and know that God is God?
q.f: God says He will be exalted among the nations.

q.q: Psalm 27 begins 'The LORD is my light and my...'
q.f: It continues: 'whom shall I fear?'

q.q: How far has God removed our transgressions from us, according to Psalm 103?
a: As far as the east is from the west
q.f: The psalm begins 'Bless the LORD, O my soul'.

q.q: In Psalm 139, how does the writer say he was made?
q.f: The psalm says God knew him before he was born.

q.q: Psalm 1 says the person who delights in God's law is like what?
a: A tree planted by streams of water
q.f: Its leaf does not wither.

q.q: What did David ask God to create in him in Psalm 51?
q.f: He wrote the psalm after Nathan confronted him.

q.q: Psalm 34 invites us to 'taste and see' that the LORD is what?
q.f: Blessed is the one who takes refuge in Him.

q.q: According to Psalm 19, what do the heavens declare?
q.f: The skies proclaim the work of His hands.

q.q: Psalm 14 says the fool says what in his heart?
q.f: Psalm 53 begins with the same words.

q.q: James says everyone should be quick to do what?
q.f: And slow to speak and slow to anger.

q.q: James compares the tongue to what, which can set a forest ablaze?
q.f: He also compares it to a ship's rudder.

q.q: What should we do if we lack wisdom, according to James?
q.f: God gives generously to all without finding fault.

q.q: What happens when we draw near to God, according to James?
a: He will draw near to us
q.f: James also calls us to purify our hearts.

q.q: James tells us to be doers of the word, and not only what?
q.f: Otherwise, he says, we deceive ourselves.

q.q: What did Jesus say not to worry about, because it will worry about itself?
q.f: Today has enough trouble of its own.

q.q: Which teaching of Jesus is often called the Golden Rule?
a: Do to others as you would have them do to you
Forgive and you will be forgiven
Ask and it will be given to you
q.f: Jesus said this sums up the Law and the Prophets.

q.q: Jesus said, 'Where your treasure is, there your ... will be also.'
q.f: He told His followers to store up treasures in heaven.

q.q: According to Jesus, what can no one serve at the same time?
q.f: You cannot serve both God and money.

q.q: Which three things remain, according to 1 Corinthians 13?
q.f: The greatest of these is love.

q.q: What does Galatians 6 say a person will reap?
q.f: God is not mocked.

q.q: What does Philippians 4 tell us to be anxious about?
q.f: Instead, bring every request to God with thanksgiving.

q.q: According to 1 Timothy 6, the love of what is a root of all kinds of evil?
q.f: Note that it is the love of money, not money itself.

q.q: Why does Hebrews tell us to show hospitality to strangers?
a: Some have entertained angels without knowing it
It is the law of Moses
q.f: Abraham once welcomed three visitors in Genesis 18.

q.q: How does 1 John 4 describe God?
q.f: Whoever does not love does not know God.

q.q: What does Romans 12 say we should overcome evil with?
q.f: Paul also quotes Proverbs about feeding a hungry enemy.

q.q: According to Micah 6:8, what does the LORD require?
a: Act justly, love mercy, walk humbly with God
Bring rams and rivers of oil
q.f: Micah was a prophet in Judah.

q.q: In Isaiah 40, those who wait on the LORD will mount up with wings like what?
q.f: They will run and not grow weary.

q.q: Lamentations says God's mercies are new when?
q.f: Great is Your faithfulness!

q.q: What did Jesus say to do for those who persecute you?
q.f: He also said, 'Love your enemies.'

q.q: What does 1 Thessalonians 5 say about prayer?
q.f: The next verse says to give thanks in every circumstance.

q.q: What does Ephesians 4 say we should not let the sun set upon?
q.f: 'Be angry, yet do not sin.'

q.q: What did Jesus promise to give all who are weary and burdened?
q.f: He said His yoke is easy and His burden is light.

q.q: Which slave did Paul send back to Philemon as a brother in Christ?
q.f: Paul asked Philemon to welcome him as he would welcome Paul himself.

q.q: Which apostle was known as 'the Zealot'?
q.f: He is a different Simon from Simon Peter.

q.q: Which respected Pharisee told the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone?
q.f: He warned that they might find themselves fighting against God.

q.q: Which eloquent teacher from Alexandria came to Ephesus?
q.f: At first he knew only the baptism of John.

q.q: Which prisoner did Pilate release instead of Jesus?
q.f: Matthew calls him a notorious prisoner.

q.q: Which servant girl answered the door when Peter knocked after escaping from prison?
q.f: She was so happy that she ran back in without opening the gate.

q.q: Which ruler had John the Baptist beheaded in prison?
q.f: At his birthday feast he had made an oath to the daughter of Herodias.

q.q: Which man in Samaria offered the apostles money for the power to give the Spirit?
q.f: Peter told him that God's gift cannot be bought with money.

q.q: Which silversmith stirred up a riot against Paul in Ephesus?
q.f: He made silver shrines of the goddess Artemis.

q.q: In which city was Paul born?
q.f: Tarsus was in Cilicia.

q.q: Whose people were 'more noble-minded' and examined the Scriptures every day?
q.f: They checked whether Paul's teaching was true.

q.q: In which town did Peter raise Tabitha to life?
q.f: Jonah had also set sail from Joppa long before.

q.q: In which city did the centurion Cornelius live?
q.f: He was a centurion of the Italian Regiment.

q.q: To which island did Barnabas sail with Mark after parting from Paul?
q.f: Barnabas himself was originally from Cyprus.

q.q: From which mountain did the disciples return to Jerusalem after Jesus was taken up?
q.f: It was a Sabbath day's journey from the city.

q.q: What did the believers begin to do when they were filled with the Spirit at Pentecost?
q.f: Visitors from many nations heard them in their own languages.

q.q: Why did Paul and Barnabas part company?
q.f: Paul later called Mark useful to his ministry (2 Timothy 4:11).

q.q: What happened to Saul for three days after meeting Jesus on the road?
a: He could not see and did not eat or drink
q.f: Then Ananias came and laid hands on him.

q.q: What were Paul and Silas doing at midnight in the Philippian jail?
q.f: The other prisoners were listening to them.

q.q: How did the first believers in Acts 2 share their possessions?
a: They gave everything to the temple
They sold everything to the Romans
q.f: They also met together and broke bread in their homes.

q.q: What did Peter see in his vision on a rooftop in Joppa?
a: A large sheet full of animals
q.f: The vision prepared him to visit the Gentile Cornelius.

q.q: What was Jesus doing in the boat when a violent storm came up?
q.f: The disciples woke Him, crying, 'Lord, save us!'

q.q: Who did Jesus say is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
a: Whoever humbles himself like a little child
q.f: He had called a little child to stand among them.

q.q: Where did the devil take Jesus to show Him all the kingdoms of the world?
q.f: Jesus answered, 'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.'

q.q: What did Jesus tell the rich young man to do with his possessions?
a: Sell them and give to the poor
q.f: The young man went away sad, because he had great wealth.

q.q: What did Jesus say about the poor widow's offering?
a: She put in more than all the others
It was too small to count
q.f: She gave all she had to live on.

q.q: In whose home in Bethany was Jesus when a woman poured nard on His head?
q.f: She broke open an alabaster jar to pour it out.

q.q: How many small coins did the poor widow put into the temple treasury?
q.f: They were small copper coins worth a fraction of a denarius.

q.q: On which day did Jesus say He would be raised to life?
q.f: He began telling His disciples this after Peter's confession.

q.q: How many times did Peter suggest he should forgive his brother?
q.f: Jesus' answer showed that forgiveness should go far beyond that.

q.q: How many basketfuls were left over after the feeding of the four thousand?
q.f: After the five thousand were fed, twelve baskets were left.

q.q: Up to what age were the boys of Bethlehem that Herod ordered killed?
q.f: He based it on the time he had learned from the Magi.

q.q: In Acts, what name was used for the followers of Jesus and their faith?
q.f: Saul wanted to arrest any men or women who belonged to the Way.

clues: My father was Terah, and my brothers were Nahor and Haran.
I left Haran when I was seventy-five years old.
God changed my name to mean 'father of many nations'.
I was ready to offer my son Isaac on a mountain in Moriah.
I gave my Egyptian servant Hagar to my husband.
God changed my name from Sarai.
I laughed when I heard I would have a son in my old age.
I was Abraham's wife and Isaac's mother.
My father Lamech hoped I would bring comfort.
I sent out a raven and then a dove.
My three sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
I built an ark and survived the great flood.
I interpreted the dreams of a cupbearer and a baker in prison.
My father loved me most because I was born in his old age.
My brothers sold me to traders for twenty shekels of silver.
Pharaoh put me in charge of all the land of Egypt.
I married Zipporah, the daughter of a priest of Midian.
I fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian.
As a baby I was hidden in a basket among the reeds of the Nile.
God spoke to me from a burning bush and sent me to lead Israel out of Egypt.
My first husband was Mahlon.
I gleaned barley in the field of Boaz.
I told my mother-in-law, 'Your God will be my God.'
I am the Moabite woman who became King David's great-grandmother.
My wife Michal let me down through a window so I could escape.
I played music to calm King Saul.
I was the youngest son of Jesse, tending the sheep.
I killed Goliath with a sling and a stone.
My mother was Bathsheba.
God appeared to me in a dream at Gibeon.
I built the temple in Jerusalem.
I asked God for wisdom to govern His people.
I was a Tishbite from Gilead.
Ravens fed me by the Brook of Cherith.
I called down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel.
I went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
I was ploughing with twelve teams of oxen when I was called.
I made an iron axe head float.
I told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan.
I asked Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.
I was given the Babylonian name Belteshazzar.
I would not defile myself with the king's food and wine.
I explained the writing on the wall to King Belshazzar.
God shut the lions' mouths when I was thrown into their den.
My other name was Hadassah.
My cousin Mordecai brought me up as his own daughter.
I became queen to King Xerxes.
I said, 'If I perish, I perish,' and went to the king to save my people.
I was the son of Amittai.
I sulked when a worm made my shade plant wither.
Sailors threw me overboard in a storm.
A great fish swallowed me for three days and nights.
An angel told my mother that no razor should touch my head.
I tore a lion apart with my bare hands.
Delilah found out the secret of my strength.
My strength left me when my hair was shaved.
I was threshing wheat in a winepress when an angel came to me.
I put out a fleece to ask God for a sign.
God cut my army down to three hundred men.
We beat the Midianites with horns, jars and torches.
I was the wife of Lappidoth.
People came to me for judgement under a palm tree.
I went into battle with Barak against Sisera.
I am a prophetess who judged Israel.
My husband Elkanah had another wife named Peninnah.
Each year I made my son a little robe.
Eli the priest thought I was drunk while I prayed.
I am the mother of the prophet Samuel.
I set up a stone and named it Ebenezer.
I grew up serving the Lord under Eli the priest.
As a boy I heard God calling my name in the night.
I anointed both Saul and David as king.
Moses changed my name from Hoshea.
I was one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan.
I led Israel across the Jordan River.
The walls of Jericho fell after we marched around the city.
Matthew names me in the family line of Jesus.
I hid two men on my roof under stalks of flax.
I tied a scarlet cord in my window.
My family was spared when Jericho fell.
I was sixty years old when my twin sons were born.
My wife Rebekah was found for me at a spring.
I was tricked into blessing my younger son.
My father Abraham almost offered me as a sacrifice.
I named the place where I dreamed Bethel.
I worked fourteen years to marry the woman I loved.
I wrestled until daybreak and was given a new name.
I took my twin brother Esau's birthright and blessing.
My brother was Laban.
I gave water to a servant and his camels at a spring.
I became the wife of Isaac.
I helped my younger son Jacob receive his father's blessing.
I was a shepherdess when I met my husband at a well.
My father gave my older sister to my husband first.
I died giving birth to Benjamin.
Jacob worked seven years for me because he loved me.
I was also called Edom.
I was a skilful hunter, a man of the field.
I sold my birthright for a bowl of stew.
I am the elder twin brother of Jacob.
My staff budded and produced almonds.
I made a golden calf while my brother was on the mountain.
I was three years older than my brother.
I was Moses' brother and spoke for him before Pharaoh.
I became leprous for a time after speaking against my brother.
I am called a prophetess.
I led the women with a tambourine after the Red Sea crossing.
I was the sister of Moses and Aaron.
I went to a medium at Endor.
I was a head taller than anyone else in Israel.
I came from the tribe of Benjamin.
Samuel anointed me as Israel's first king.
I climbed a cliff with my armour-bearer to attack the Philistines.
I gave my robe, sword and bow to my friend.
My father was King Saul.
I was David's closest friend.
I was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
I wept when I heard that Jerusalem's walls were broken down.
I inspected the ruined walls at night.
I led the rebuilding of the walls in fifty-two days.
I lived in the land of Uz.
I had seven sons and three daughters.
My friends Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar came to comfort me.
I lost nearly everything, yet I said, 'Blessed be the name of the LORD.'
My helper Baruch wrote my words on a scroll.
I was lowered into a muddy cistern.
When God called me, I said I was only a child.
I wished my eyes were a fountain of tears for my people.
I was the son of Amoz.
In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord on a throne.
A burning coal touched my lips.
I said, 'Here am I. Send me!'
I was a priest, the son of Buzi.
God told me to eat a scroll.
I saw visions by the River Kebar.
I saw a valley of dry bones come to life.
I dreamed of a great statue.
For a time I ate grass like an ox.
I had a furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.
I was the king of Babylon who took Daniel into exile.
At the cross, Jesus gave me into the care of the disciple He loved.
I hurried to visit my relative Elizabeth.
The angel Gabriel visited me in Nazareth.
I am the mother of Jesus.
Matthew says my father was Jacob.
An angel spoke to me in dreams.
I took my family to Egypt to escape King Herod.
I was the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus.
I was a descendant of Aaron.
My husband could not speak until our son was named.
My baby leapt inside me when Mary greeted me.
I am the mother of John the Baptist.
My father was a priest named Zechariah.
I wore camel's hair and ate locusts and wild honey.
I called myself 'a voice of one calling in the wilderness'.
I baptised Jesus in the Jordan.
Jesus healed my mother-in-law of a fever.
I walked on water until I saw the wind and began to sink.
I denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed.
Jesus gave me the name Cephas, meaning rock.
My father was Zebedee.
Jesus called my brother and me 'Sons of Thunder'.
Peter and I were going to the temple when a lame man was healed.
My brother was James, and we were fishermen.
I was also called Didymus.
I said, 'Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.'
I said I would not believe unless I saw the nail marks.
When I saw the risen Jesus I said, 'My Lord and my God!'
I kept the disciples' money bag.
I complained that costly perfume should have been sold for the poor.
I was paid thirty pieces of silver.
I betrayed Jesus with a kiss.
I said, 'I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God.'
I warned that my brother had been in the tomb four days.
I was busy serving while my sister sat at Jesus' feet.
My brother Lazarus and sister Mary lived with me in Bethany.
Seven demons had gone out of me.
I stood near the cross of Jesus.
At the empty tomb I thought the risen Jesus was the gardener.
When Jesus said my name, I called Him 'Rabboni'.
The chief priests plotted to kill me too.
My sisters sent word to Jesus that I was sick.
Jesus wept when He came to Bethany after I died.
Jesus called me out of the tomb after four days.
I lived in Jericho.
I was a chief tax collector and very wealthy.
I was too short to see Jesus over the crowd.
I climbed a tree, and Jesus came to my house.
I brought myrrh and aloes to bury Jesus.
I was a Pharisee and a leader of the Jews.
I came to Jesus at night.
Jesus told me that I must be born again.
My wife warned me about a dream.
I asked, 'What is truth?'
I washed my hands in front of the crowd.
I was the Roman governor who handed Jesus over to be crucified.
I was born in Tarsus and taught by Gamaliel.
I was a tentmaker by trade.
A light from heaven blinded me on the road to Damascus.
I wrote many letters to the early churches.
I was a Levite from Cyprus.
I sold a field and gave the money to the apostles.
I brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem.
My name means 'Son of Encouragement'.
I was chosen as one of seven men to serve the church.
I was full of grace and power.
I saw heaven open and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand.
I was stoned to death while a young man named Saul watched.
My mother was Jewish and my father was Greek.
I joined Paul at Lystra.
My mother Eunice and grandmother Lois had sincere faith.
Paul called me his true child in the faith.
I came from the city of Thyatira.
I sold purple cloth.
I heard Paul speak by a river outside Philippi.
After my household was baptised, I invited Paul to stay at my house.
My husband and I had to leave Rome.
We were tentmakers, like Paul.
We explained the way of God more accurately to Apollos.
I am the wife of Aquila.
I lived to be 930 years old.
I gave names to all the livestock and birds.
God formed me from the dust of the ground.
I was the first man, and my wife was Eve.
I named my son Seth.
God made me from a rib taken from the man.
I said, 'The serpent deceived me.'
I was the first woman, called the mother of all the living.
I worked the soil.
God had no regard for my offering.
I asked, 'Am I my brother's keeper?'
I killed my brother Abel.
I became the father of Methuselah.
I lived 365 years.
I walked with God.
I was no more, because God took me away.
I was from the tribe of Judah.
At eighty-five I was given Hebron as my inheritance.
I said, 'We can certainly conquer the land!'
Only Joshua and I of our generation were allowed to enter the Promised Land.
My first husband was a Calebite.
I loaded donkeys with bread, wine, raisins and figs.
I stopped David from taking revenge.
After Nabal died, I became David's wife.
I was the daughter of Eliam.
My first husband was Uriah the Hittite.
Nathan the prophet came to me when Adonijah tried to become king.
I am the mother of King Solomon.
My husband Elimelech died in Moab.
My sons Mahlon and Chilion died too.
I told the women of Bethlehem to call me Mara.
My daughter-in-law Ruth refused to leave me.
Matthew says my mother was Rahab.
I was a relative from the clan of Elimelech.
I let a Moabite widow glean in my fields.
I married Ruth.
I broke up the bronze snake that Moses had made.
I spread a threatening letter out before the LORD.
As a sign, a shadow went back ten steps.
God added fifteen years to my life.
My mother was Jedidah.
I kept a Passover like none since the days of the judges.
I tore my clothes when the Book of the Law was read to me.
I became king when I was eight years old.
I sat at the king's gate in Susa.
I uncovered a plot to kill King Xerxes.
I would not bow down to Haman.
I brought up my cousin Esther.
I was commander of the army of Aram.
A young girl from Israel served my wife.
I was angry when I was told to wash in the Jordan.
My leprosy was healed after I dipped seven times.
I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
A tired army commander ran to my tent.
When he asked for water, I gave him milk.
I killed Sisera with a tent peg.
I was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses.
I came up to Jerusalem from Babylon.
I read the Book of the Law aloud from daybreak until noon.
The book about my work comes just before Nehemiah.
I was the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher.
I was a widow until the age of eighty-four.
I never left the temple, worshipping night and day.
I was a prophetess who gave thanks when I saw baby Jesus.
I was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
The Holy Spirit told me I would see the Lord's Christ before I died.
I told Mary that a sword would pierce her soul.
I took baby Jesus in my arms in the temple and blessed God.
I was a priest of the division of Abijah.
An angel appeared to me beside the altar of incense.
I could not speak because I did not believe the angel.
I wrote on a tablet, 'His name is John.'
Believers gathered to pray at my mother's house in Jerusalem.
I left Paul and Barnabas at Perga and went back to Jerusalem.
Paul and Barnabas disagreed sharply about taking me along.
I was Barnabas's cousin.
I had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
I was one of the seven chosen to serve the church.
I preached about the Christ in a city of Samaria.
I explained Isaiah to an Ethiopian official and baptised him.
I was a centurion of the Italian Regiment.
I was devout and gave generously to the people.
An angel told me to send to Joppa for Simon Peter.
The Holy Spirit fell on my household while Peter was speaking.
My father's name was Timaeus.
I sat begging beside the road at Jericho.
When people told me to be quiet, I cried out all the louder.
Jesus said, 'Your faith has healed you,' and I could see.
I was a leader of the synagogue.
I fell at Jesus' feet and begged Him to come to my house.
On the way, a woman was healed by touching Jesus' cloak.
Jesus raised my twelve-year-old daughter.
I came from Gath.
I was over six cubits tall.
For forty days I challenged Israel's army morning and evening.
A young shepherd killed me with a sling and a stone.
I was an Egyptian servant.
I ran away and an angel found me by a spring in the desert.
I called the LORD 'the God who sees me'.
I was the mother of Ishmael.

said.s: Let there be light
Am I my brother's keeper?
The serpent deceived me
This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh
Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden?'
Let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens
Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?
Is anything too difficult for the LORD?
God has made me laugh
You are the God who sees me
Where is the lamb for the burnt offering?
God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.
Let me eat some of that red stew, for I am famished.
I will not let you go unless you bless me.
Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.
What you intended against me for evil, God intended for good
I drew him out of the water.
Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh
I AM WHO I AM.
Who is the LORD that I should obey His voice and let Israel go?
Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted
What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?
We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!
As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!
Has not the LORD gone before you?
If you will go with me, I will go
A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!
Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.
Let me die with the Philistines.
Do not urge me to leave you or to turn from following you.
Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.
May the LORD repay your work, and may you receive a rich reward from the LORD
Speak, for Your servant is listening.
The glory has departed from Israel
Thus far the LORD has helped us.
Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.
There is still the youngest
Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts
Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.
The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD's anointed.
How the mighty have fallen!
You are that man!
O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!
Give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people
How long will you waver between two opinions?
The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!
Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.
Please, let me inherit a double portion of your spirit
Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?
Those who are with us are more than those who are with them.
I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!
If only You would bless me and enlarge my territory!
Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
Who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
And if I perish, I perish!
The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.
Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!
